title: A Mac session can pick up merged claude-settings work without auto mode refusing the reinstall
why: Build advisor finding, Oct 27 04:25 CDT: the Mac's auto mode refused a claude-settings reinstall as "Self-Modification", so a Mac session cannot pick up merged work by reinstalling.
note: Measured Oct 27 09:18 CDT (Mac, local liaison): the Mac does not pick up merges. Its pin (~/Developer/claude-settings-live) sits at 2ad85de6 while main is d4e1b86b. The SessionStart hook runs, also under Remote Control, but install_from_main.sh exits 1 ("the pinned checkout has tracked changes") on every start. Cause: ~/.claude/settings.json links into the pin, and whatever saves a setting (app or CLI, unconfirmed) rewrites it with keys reordered and no value changed, which dirties the pin. Fix (cloud lane, with the build advisor): the installer treats a settings.json equal to HEAD's as parsed JSON as clean, or settings.json stops linking into the pin; red first on a reordered file. Then a one-time Mac unblock (restore the pin's settings.json), or no fix can reach it. The auto-mode "Self-Modification" refusal only bites a manual mid-session reinstall, which this makes unneeded. Brief: briefs/c119-mac-picks-up-merges.md. Needs no answer. Port: no; it is claude-settings' own installer. Placed ahead of c107 (triage, Oct 27): every merged fix waits on it to reach your Mac.
ask:
# c119: does a Mac session pick up merged claude-settings work with no manual reinstall?

Local liaison, Oct 27, against claude-settings main d4e1b86b. Mac session, measurement only: no
reinstall by hand, no settings edit, no ask to the owner.

Today: the SessionStart (startup|resume) hook fetches origin/main, fast-forwards local main, and runs
merge/install_from_main.sh in the background when the pin is behind. It exits at once when
CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is set. It logs failures to ~/.claude/claude-settings-install.log.

1. Read the pin: the path in the first `@<path>/CLAUDE.md` line of ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Record
   `git -C <pin> rev-parse HEAD` and `git -C <pin> rev-parse origin/main` after a fetch, plus the
   last 10 lines of the install log.
2. Record whether CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is set in this session's environment, and to what. If it is
   set, Remote Control sessions never auto-pull: say so.
3. Start one fresh headless session from $HOME: `claude -p "reply ok" --max-turns 1`. Wait 3 min,
   then read the pin HEAD and the log again. If auto mode refuses the start, give the exact refusal.
4. Report in 8 lines: pin before and after, whether it reached origin/main, new log lines,
   CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE, and any refusal text.
